title: O-NET ม.6 ชุดฝึกที่ 3

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกข้อความที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่างแต่ละช่อง
groups.title: A part-time job interview

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kanya
dialogue.text: Thanks for coming in, Ploy. Please have a seat. So, why would you like to work in our aquarium gift shop?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kanya
dialogue.text: That's good to hear. The weekend shift starts at 7 a.m. Would that be a problem?

dialogue.speaker: Ploy
dialogue.text: Not at all. I'm an early riser, and the bus from my place runs every fifteen minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kanya
dialogue.text: Great. Have you ever had to deal with difficult customers?

dialogue.speaker: Ploy
dialogue.text: ___2___ At my aunt's noodle stall, I learned to stay calm and listen first.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kanya
dialogue.text: Excellent. We'll let you know by Friday. Do you have any questions for me?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kanya
dialogue.text: Yes. All new staff do two days of paid training before their first shift.

options: My best friend already works here, so I don't really need the job.
Honestly, I work best when nobody tells me what I should be doing.
I'd prefer to start next year, if that's all right with you.
I've visited this aquarium since I was small, and I love talking about sea life.
I heard the job is easy and nobody checks on the staff.
items.explanationTh: ผู้สัมภาษณ์ถามเหตุผลที่อยากทำงาน และตอบรับว่า "That's good to hear." คำตอบที่ดีต้องแสดงความสนใจในงานอย่างเหมาะสม คือมาเที่ยวพิพิธภัณฑ์สัตว์น้ำนี้ตั้งแต่เด็กและชอบเล่าเรื่องสัตว์ทะเล ตัวเลือกอื่นทำให้ภาพลักษณ์ผู้สมัครเสีย

options: Yes, quite a few times, actually.
Sorry, could you speak up a bit?
No, I always try to avoid them.
It depends on the weather, really.
Not yet, but I'm a quick learner.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคถัดมา Ploy เล่าประสบการณ์ที่ร้านก๋วยเตี๋ยวของป้าว่าเรียนรู้ที่จะใจเย็น แสดงว่าเคยเจอลูกค้ายากมาแล้ว จึงต้องตอบว่า "Yes, quite a few times" ส่วน "Not yet" ขัดกับประสบการณ์ที่เล่า

options: How much training have I already finished?
Can I bring my own customers to the shop?
Will there be any training before I start?
Do I have to work on Friday evenings as well?
Why did you decide to choose me for the job?
items.explanationTh: คำตอบของผู้สัมภาษณ์คือ "All new staff do two days of paid training" จึงต้องเป็นคำถามเรื่องการฝึกอบรมก่อนเริ่มงาน ส่วน "Why did you choose me" ผิดเพราะยังไม่ได้ประกาศผล

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกข้อความที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่างแต่ละช่อง
groups.title: At the lost property office

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. How can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: I left my backpack on the 2:15 train from Ayutthaya. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.text: Let me check our records. Can you describe it?

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: It's dark green, with a small yellow keyring shaped like a cat.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.text: ___2___ Is this one yours?

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: Yes, that's it! Thank you so much.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.text: You're welcome. ___3___ It's just to confirm that the bag belongs to you.

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: Sure. Here's my student card.

options: Did you leave yours there too?
Should I take the next train?
Where can I buy a new one?
Could you hand it in for me?
Has anyone handed one in?
items.explanationTh: Nat มาที่แผนกของหาย และเจ้าหน้าที่ตอบว่า "Let me check our records" จึงต้องเป็นคำถามว่ามีคนนำกระเป๋ามาส่งหรือไม่ (hand in = นำมาส่งคืน)

options: Sorry, nothing has come in today.
You really should be more careful.
Hold on, we've got something like that.
I'm afraid you'll need to describe it.
Please could you call back tomorrow?
items.explanationTh: หลังช่องว่าง เจ้าหน้าที่ถามต่อว่า "Is this one yours?" แสดงว่าพบกระเป๋าที่คล้ายกัน "nothing has come in" จึงขัดแย้ง และ Nat ก็บรรยายลักษณะกระเป๋าไปแล้ว

options: May I keep it for one more day?
Could you tell me your seat number?
Could I see some ID, please?
Would you like a new ticket, then?
Would you mind waiting outside?
items.explanationTh: เจ้าหน้าที่บอกว่าต้องการยืนยันว่ากระเป๋าเป็นของ Nat และ Nat ยื่นบัตรนักเรียนให้ จึงต้องเป็นการขอดูบัตรแสดงตน (ID) บัตรนักเรียนไม่ได้ตอบคำถามเรื่องเลขที่นั่ง

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกข้อความที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่างแต่ละช่อง
groups.title: Planning a class presentation

dialogue.speaker: Ice
dialogue.text: Our presentation on traditional Thai toys is due on Monday. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Ton
dialogue.text: How about I do the research, and you design the slides?

dialogue.speaker: Ice
dialogue.text: Sounds fair. But I'm hopeless at design.

dialogue.speaker: Ton
dialogue.text: ___2___ We can use the free templates on the school computers.

dialogue.speaker: Ice
dialogue.text: Good idea. When shall we meet to put it all together?

dialogue.speaker: Ice
dialogue.text: Saturday afternoon works for me. See you in the library, then.

options: Have you finished your part yet?
Why did you pick this topic?
Who told you about the presentation?
Can we hand it in a bit late?
How should we divide the work?
items.explanationTh: Ton ตอบโดยเสนอการแบ่งงาน ("I do the research, and you design the slides") จึงต้องเป็นคำถามว่าจะแบ่งงานกันอย่างไร

options: You're right, it'll look terrible.
I'm glad you enjoy it so much.
Then I'll have to do it all myself.
That doesn't really matter.
Then you'd better start practising.
items.explanationTh: Ton บอกต่อว่า "We can use the free templates" แสดงว่ากำลังปลอบว่าการออกแบบไม่เก่งไม่ใช่ปัญหาและจะช่วยกันทำ ส่วน "I'll have to do it all myself" ขัดกับคำว่า we

options: We met last Saturday afternoon.
I met her on Saturday afternoon.
It took me all Saturday afternoon.
Are you free on Saturday afternoon?
I'm busy every afternoon this week.
items.explanationTh: Ice ตอบว่า "Saturday afternoon works for me" จึงต้องเป็นคำถามชวน/เสนอเวลาบ่ายวันเสาร์ ส่วน "busy every afternoon" ขัดกับการนัดเจอ

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกข้อความที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่างแต่ละช่อง
groups.title: Changing a hostel booking

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Riverside Hostel, Mali speaking. How may I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Jake
dialogue.text: Hi, I have a booking for two nights from the 14th. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Certainly. What dates would you like instead?

dialogue.speaker: Jake
dialogue.text: The 16th and 17th, if possible.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: ___2___ Hmm, your private room is free on the 16th, but we only have a dorm bed left on the 17th.

dialogue.speaker: Jake
dialogue.text: That's fine. I don't mind sharing a room for one night.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: All right, it's done. ___3___

dialogue.speaker: Jake
dialogue.text: No, that's everything. Thanks for your help.

options: I'm calling to change the dates.
I'd like to cancel it completely.
I'm calling to complain about my room.
I'd like to pay for it in advance.
Could you tell me where you are?
items.explanationTh: พนักงานถามว่า "What dates would you like instead?" คำว่า instead แสดงว่า Jake ต้องการเปลี่ยนวันที่ ไม่ใช่ยกเลิกหรือร้องเรียน

options: Those dates are completely free.
Let me just check for you.
You will need to pay in cash.
Sorry, we're fully booked then.
Then I'll cancel your booking.
items.explanationTh: หลังช่องว่าง พนักงานแจ้งห้องที่ว่างในแต่ละคืน จึงต้องเป็นการขอเวลาตรวจสอบก่อน "fully booked" และ "completely free" ขัดกับข้อมูลที่ว่าเหลือแค่เตียงหอพักรวมในคืนที่ 17

options: Would you like to make a complaint?
Is that your final offer, then?
What time did you arrive last night?
Did you enjoy your stay with us?
Is there anything else I can do for you?
items.explanationTh: Jake ตอบว่า "No, that's everything." ซึ่งเป็นคำตอบของคำถามว่ามีอะไรให้ช่วยอีกไหม ส่วน "Did you enjoy your stay?" ไม่เหมาะเพราะเขายังไม่ได้มาพัก

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกข้อความที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่างแต่ละช่อง
groups.title: Asking a teacher for help

dialogue.speaker: Arm
dialogue.text: Excuse me, Ms. Pranee. Do you have a minute?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Pranee
dialogue.text: Of course, Arm. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: Arm
dialogue.text: I'm applying to the engineering programme at Chaloem University. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Pranee
dialogue.text: I'd be happy to. When's the deadline?

dialogue.speaker: Arm
dialogue.text: The end of next month, but I'd like to send everything early.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Pranee
dialogue.text: ___2___ Could you email me a list of your school activities so that I can mention them?

dialogue.speaker: Arm
dialogue.text: ___3___ Thank you so much, Ms. Pranee.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Pranee
dialogue.text: You're welcome. Good luck!

options: Would you mind writing me a recommendation letter?
Could you tell me how to get to the campus?
Could you lend me your old engineering textbook?
Have you ever studied engineering yourself?
Would you mind applying to the programme with me?
items.explanationTh: ครูตอบรับและถามกำหนดส่ง จากนั้นขอรายการกิจกรรม "so that I can mention them" แสดงว่าครูจะเขียนจดหมายรับรองให้

options: That's very sensible of you.
I'm afraid it's already too late.
I've never heard of that university.
So you've already been accepted?
You'd better wait until next year.
items.explanationTh: Arm บอกว่าอยากส่งเอกสารก่อนกำหนด ครูจึงชมว่าเป็นความคิดที่รอบคอบ (sensible) ส่วน "too late" ขัดกับที่กำหนดส่งคือสิ้นเดือนหน้า

options: I'd rather you didn't mention them.
No, I don't use email at all.
Sure, I'll send it tonight.
Sorry, I've never done any activities.
Sure, as soon as I've been accepted.
items.explanationTh: ครูขอรายการกิจกรรมเพื่อใช้เขียนจดหมายรับรอง และ Arm ขอบคุณต่อ จึงต้องตอบรับว่าจะส่งคืนนี้ ส่วน "as soon as I've been accepted" ไม่สมเหตุผลเพราะจดหมายต้องใช้ก่อนสมัคร

groups.instructionTh: อ่านประกาศ/ข้อความต่อไปนี้ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Gym notice
groups.text:
PEAKFORM COMMUNITY GYM — RULES FOR ALL MEMBERS
Welcome! To keep the gym safe and pleasant for everyone, please follow these rules.
• Scan your membership card at the entrance every time you visit. Cards may not be lent to friends or family.
• Members aged 15–17 may use the gym only between 3 p.m. and 7 p.m. on weekdays, and must complete a free induction session with a trainer first.
• Wipe down every machine after use. Spray bottles and paper towels are next to the water fountain.
• Return all weights to the racks. Never drop dumbbells on the floor.
• Clean, indoor-only trainers are required. Outdoor shoes damage the flooring.
• Please limit your time on cardio machines to 30 minutes when others are waiting.
• Lockers are for use during your visit only. Items left overnight will be removed and kept at reception for 7 days.
Questions? Ask any member of staff in a blue shirt.

items.stem: What is the main purpose of this notice?
options: To advertise new machines to the public
To announce new opening hours
To warn members about higher fees
To explain how members should behave
To invite teenagers to a free class
items.explanationTh: ประกาศมีหัวข้อ "RULES FOR ALL MEMBERS" และบอกว่า "please follow these rules" จุดประสงค์จึงเป็นการแจ้งกฎการปฏิบัติตัวของสมาชิก

items.stem: Sompong is 16 and has just joined the gym. Which of the following is he allowed to do?
options: Work out at 5 p.m. on a Tuesday after his induction
Train on Saturday morning if he scans his card
Use his older brother's card on busy days
Use the machines at 8 p.m. on a Wednesday
Skip the induction because he is over 15
items.explanationTh: สมาชิกอายุ 15–17 ปีใช้ได้เฉพาะ 15.00–19.00 น. ในวันธรรมดา และต้องผ่าน induction ก่อน วันอังคาร 17.00 น. หลังผ่าน induction จึงเป็นตัวเลือกเดียวที่ทำได้

items.stem: The word "induction" in the notice is closest in meaning to
options: a fitness competition
an introductory session
a medical check-up
a membership card
an entrance fee
items.explanationTh: "a free induction session with a trainer" ที่ต้องทำก่อนเริ่มใช้ยิม หมายถึงการแนะนำการใช้งานเบื้องต้น และคำว่า free บอกว่าไม่ใช่ค่าธรรมเนียม

items.stem: What will most likely happen to a bag left in a locker until the next morning?
options: Its owner will lose his or her card.
Its owner will have to pay a fine.
It will be thrown away at once.
Staff will take it to reception.
It will stay in the locker for a week.
items.explanationTh: ประกาศระบุว่า "Items left overnight will be removed and kept at reception for 7 days" ของจึงถูกย้ายไปเก็บที่เคาน์เตอร์ ไม่ใช่อยู่ในล็อกเกอร์ 7 วัน

groups.instructionTh: อ่านประกาศ/ข้อความต่อไปนี้ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Product label
groups.text:
GREENSIP SELF-WATERING POT — How to use
1. Push the cotton wick through the hole in the inner pot before adding soil.
2. Fill the inner pot with soil and plant as usual. Water the soil from above ONCE to help the roots settle.
3. From then on, add water only through the filling tube on the side, until the red float rises to the FULL line.
4. Refill when the float drops to the bottom — usually every 10–14 days, depending on the plant and the room temperature.
Not suitable for cacti or other plants that prefer dry soil.
Keep out of direct afternoon sun, as the water may become too warm.
Outer pot: dishwasher-safe. Inner pot: hand wash only.

items.stem: According to the label, when should the soil be watered from the top?
options: Never — only through the tube
Whenever the room is very warm
Every 10 to 14 days
Whenever the float reaches FULL
Only once, right after planting
items.explanationTh: ข้อ 2 บอกว่า "Water the soil from above ONCE to help the roots settle" คือรดจากด้านบนครั้งเดียวหลังปลูก หลังจากนั้นเติมผ่านท่อด้านข้างเท่านั้น

items.stem: What does the red float show?
options: Whether the soil is too dry for cacti
Which pot can go in the dishwasher
How warm the water has become
When the plant needs more sunlight
How much water is left in the pot
items.explanationTh: ให้เติมน้ำจนทุ่นสีแดงขึ้นถึงขีด FULL และเติมใหม่เมื่อทุ่นลงถึงก้น แสดงว่าทุ่นบอกระดับน้ำที่เหลืออยู่

items.stem: Who should NOT buy this pot?
options: Someone who grows herbs indoors
Someone who often travels for a week
Someone who forgets to water plants
Someone who grows desert cacti
Someone who owns a dishwasher
items.explanationTh: ฉลากระบุว่า "Not suitable for cacti or other plants that prefer dry soil" คนปลูกกระบองเพชรจึงไม่ควรซื้อ ส่วนคนที่ไม่อยู่บ้านหรือขี้ลืมรดน้ำกลับได้ประโยชน์

items.stem: Why might the pot need refilling sooner than every 10 days?
options: The wick was put in before the soil.
The outer pot went in the dishwasher.
The inner pot was washed by hand.
The soil was watered from above once.
The room it is in is very hot.
items.explanationTh: ฉลากบอกว่าระยะเวลาเติมน้ำขึ้นอยู่กับ "the plant and the room temperature" ห้องที่ร้อนมากจึงทำให้น้ำหมดเร็วกว่าปกติ

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความต่อไปนี้ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: An email from abroad
groups.text:
Subject: Greetings from Harlow Bay!

Dear Ms. Wanida,

I hope you and everyone in the English club are well. I've now been in Harlow Bay for seven weeks, and I finally feel settled enough to write properly.

To be honest, the first fortnight was harder than I expected. Everyone spoke so quickly, and I kept nodding even when I had no idea what they meant. My host mother, Ruth, noticed this and gave me some advice I'll never forget: "Asking someone to repeat themselves isn't rude. Pretending to understand is far riskier." After that, I started saying "Sorry, could you say that again?" — and people were always happy to help.

School here is quite different from home. Classes are smaller, and teachers expect us to argue for our opinions out loud, which still makes me nervous. On the other hand, I've joined the rowing team, which practises at six in the morning, three days a week. I never imagined I'd choose to get up before sunrise!

Next month our class is cooking a "world dinner" for the parents, and I've been asked to make green curry. The problem is that I can't find Thai basil anywhere, so I may have to use the ordinary kind. Could you ask Khun Sudarat in the canteen whether that will spoil the taste? She'll know.

Please say hello to the club for me. I'll send photos soon.

Best wishes,
Fern

items.stem: What is Fern's main reason for writing?
options: To share her news and ask a small favour
To complain about her unhelpful host family
To invite her teacher to the world dinner
To ask if she can come home earlier
To explain why she has stopped rowing
items.explanationTh: Fern เล่าชีวิตที่ต่างประเทศ (เรื่องภาษา โรงเรียน ทีมพายเรือ) และขอให้ครูช่วยถามคุณสุดารัตน์เรื่องใบโหระพา จึงเป็นการเล่าข่าวและขอความช่วยเหลือเล็กน้อย

items.stem: What can be inferred about Fern when she first arrived?
options: She found lessons much easier than in Thailand.
She was too shy to talk to her host mother.
She often pretended to understand when she didn't.
She asked people to repeat things all the time.
She got up before sunrise every single day.
items.explanationTh: Fern เขียนว่า "I kept nodding even when I had no idea what they meant" คือแกล้งทำเป็นเข้าใจ เธอเพิ่งเริ่มขอให้คนพูดซ้ำหลังได้คำแนะนำจาก Ruth

items.stem: The word "fortnight" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: two weeks
a long night
a school term
seven weeks
a short holiday
items.explanationTh: fortnight แปลว่าสองสัปดาห์ บริบทคือช่วงแรกของการอยู่ 7 สัปดาห์ จึงไม่ใช่ seven weeks ทั้งหมด

items.stem: Which statement about school in Harlow Bay is TRUE?
options: Teachers rarely ask students to speak out loud.
The rowing team practises every single morning.
Classes are bigger than the ones in Thailand.
Fern no longer feels nervous during lessons.
Students are expected to give their views in class.
items.explanationTh: Fern เขียนว่า "teachers expect us to argue for our opinions out loud" ส่วนห้องเรียนเล็กกว่า ทีมพายเรือซ้อม 3 วันต่อสัปดาห์ และเธอยังรู้สึกประหม่าอยู่

items.stem: Why does Fern want Ms. Wanida to speak to Khun Sudarat?
options: To ask her to send Thai basil abroad
To check if ordinary basil is acceptable
To invite her to cook at the dinner
To get a complete green curry recipe
To find out where Thai basil is sold
items.explanationTh: Fern หาใบโหระพาไทยไม่ได้ อาจต้องใช้ใบโหระพาธรรมดา จึงอยากถามว่า "whether that will spoil the taste" คือจะทำให้รสชาติเสียหรือไม่

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความต่อไปนี้ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: A blog post
groups.text:
Second Spin: Fixing Bikes, One Soi at a Time
Posted by Krit, 17

Last March, the chain on my old mountain bike snapped on the way to school. The repair shop near my house wanted 450 baht to fix it, which was more than I had. So instead, I watched a few online tutorials, borrowed my uncle's toolbox and repaired it myself in an afternoon. It wasn't pretty — I got grease all over Mum's doorstep — but it worked.

That small success gave me an idea. Our soi is full of bicycles that nobody rides any more: flat tyres, rusty brakes, missing pedals. I put a handwritten sign on our gate: "Free bike check-ups, Saturdays 9–12. Bring your bike, bring a snack." The first weekend, only Grandpa Somchai from next door turned up. By June, I had a queue.

I don't charge for my time, but people pay for any parts I need to buy. Some neighbours also give me bikes they no longer want. I fix those up and pass them on to younger kids in the community who otherwise couldn't afford one. So far, eleven bikes have found new owners.

What have I learned? Patience, mostly. Some problems take three Saturdays to solve. I've also discovered that people love to chat while they wait, so I now know far more about my neighbours than I used to!

Next term, my school has asked me to run a lunchtime repair workshop. I'm nervous about teaching, but if I can bring a 30-year-old bike back to life, I can probably explain how I did it.

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความต่อไปนี้ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: The Wrong Bus
groups.text:
Tao checked the time again: 7:42. His university entrance interview at Mae Rim Campus began at 9:00, and the bus ride usually took forty minutes. Plenty of time, he told himself, as he climbed onto the first blue bus that pulled in.

It was only when the bus turned onto the highway instead of crossing the river that his stomach dropped. He had taken the 52, not the 25.

He hurried to the front. "Excuse me," he said to the driver, trying to keep his voice steady. "Does this bus go anywhere near Mae Rim?"

The driver shook his head. "Opposite direction, I'm afraid."

An elderly woman with a basket of mangoes had been listening. "Get off at the next stop," she said calmly. "My nephew drives a songthaew from there. He passes the campus every morning."

Tao hesitated. He had been told a hundred times not to go along with strangers' plans. But the woman simply took out her phone, made a short call and showed him the screen: a photo of a red songthaew with a sign reading "Mae Rim – Campus".

Twelve minutes later, he was sitting in the back of that very vehicle. He arrived at 8:51, out of breath, his shirt sticking to his back.

The interview went well. Near the end, one of the professors asked, "What's the biggest problem you've solved recently?"

Tao smiled. "Well," he began, "this morning I got on the wrong bus…"

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความต่อไปนี้ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Quiet or noisy?
groups.text:
Quiet or Noisy: Where Do Students Study Best?

Ask ten students where they study best and you might get ten different answers. Some insist on total silence; others cannot concentrate without the hum of a busy café. A small survey by the student council of Phrom Witthaya School suggests that both groups may be right, depending on the task.

The council asked 240 students to rate how productive they felt in three places: the school library, the canteen at lunchtime and a café with soft background music. For memorising vocabulary or solving maths problems, 68 per cent preferred the library. For creative work such as designing posters or brainstorming essay ideas, however, more than half chose the café.

Why might sound help creativity? One explanation is that a moderate level of noise distracts the brain just enough to make it think more broadly, instead of focusing narrowly on one idea. Loud noise, by contrast, seems to harm almost every kind of work. Only 9 per cent of students said they could do anything useful in the canteen at lunchtime.

The council admits that its survey has limits. It measured how productive students felt, not their actual results, and all the participants came from one school. Even so, the findings have already led to a change: the library now has a "low-chat zone" on its second floor, where quiet conversation and soft music are allowed.

The lesson may be simple. Instead of searching for one perfect study spot, students could choose their surroundings to suit the job in front of them.

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความต่อไปนี้ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Bows, wais and handshakes
groups.text:
Bows, Wais and Handshakes

When two people meet, the first few seconds often say a great deal about respect. In Japan, the most common greeting is the bow. A quick, slight bow of about 15 degrees is used between friends or colleagues of similar status. A deeper bow of around 30 degrees shows respect to a teacher, a customer or a senior manager, while a very deep bow of 45 degrees or more is usually saved for a sincere apology or deep gratitude. Men generally keep their hands at their sides, while women often place them together in front. Interestingly, many Japanese people bow even while talking on the phone, which shows how naturally the gesture has become part of daily life.

In Southeast Asia, greetings vary from country to country. In Thailand, the wai, in which the palms are pressed together and the head is lowered slightly, is used to say hello, thank you or goodbye. The higher the hands are held, the more respect is shown, and it is usually the younger person who offers the wai first. In Cambodia and Laos, similar gestures known as the sampeah and the nop are used. In the Philippines, some young people greet older relatives with the mano, gently pressing the back of the elder's hand to their own forehead. Meanwhile, in Singapore and in business settings across the region, a light handshake is common.

For visitors, the safest strategy is to watch and follow. A foreigner who returns a wai with a smile, or bows slightly in Tokyo, is rarely judged harshly for small mistakes. What matters most is not perfect technique but showing that you have noticed, and respected, local ways.

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความต่อไปนี้ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: The body's defence team
groups.text:
Your Body's Defence Team

Every day, your body comes into contact with millions of microbes, tiny living things such as bacteria and viruses. Most are harmless, but some can make you ill. The immune system is the body's way of recognising these invaders and removing them.

The first line of defence is a set of physical barriers. Your skin acts like a wall, while the sticky mucus in your nose and throat traps particles before they can travel deeper. Acid in the stomach destroys many of the microbes found in food.

If a microbe gets past these barriers, the second line of defence goes to work. White blood cells called phagocytes move towards the area and swallow the invaders. This response is fast but general: phagocytes attack almost anything that looks foreign, without "knowing" exactly what it is. The redness and warmth sometimes seen around a cut are signs that this activity is taking place.

The third line of defence is slower but far more precise. White blood cells called lymphocytes identify particular features on the surface of a microbe, known as antigens. Some lymphocytes then produce antibodies, Y-shaped proteins that fit onto one specific antigen, rather like a key fits a lock. Once attached, antibodies make the microbe easier for other cells to destroy.

What makes this third line so remarkable is its memory. After an infection, some lymphocytes remain in the body as "memory cells". If the same microbe returns, these cells recognise it, and the body can respond much more quickly than it did the first time.

Scientists are still discovering how these defences communicate with one another, but the basic idea is clear: the body protects itself in layers, from simple walls to highly specialised cells.

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How people can avoid common illnesses

items.explanationTh: บทความอธิบายแนวป้องกัน 3 ชั้นของร่างกาย และสรุปว่า "the body protects itself in layers" ส่วนเชื้อโรคส่วนใหญ่ "are harmless"

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความต่อไปนี้ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Noise-cancelling headphones
groups.text:
How Do Noise-Cancelling Headphones Work?

Sit on a long flight wearing noise-cancelling headphones, and the steady roar of the engines seems to fade away. It feels almost like magic, but the trick is pure physics.

Sound travels as a wave of pressure. Air particles are pushed together, creating areas of high pressure, and then pulled apart, creating areas of low pressure. When two sound waves meet, they combine. If the high points of one wave line up with the high points of another, the sound becomes louder. But if the high points of one wave meet the low points of another, the two waves cancel each other out. Scientists call this destructive interference.

Active noise-cancelling headphones make use of this principle. A tiny microphone on the outside of each ear cup "listens" to the noise around you. A chip inside then creates an "anti-noise" wave, an exact mirror image of the incoming sound, and plays it through the speaker together with your music. When the noise and the anti-noise meet, much of the unwanted sound vanishes.

The technology works best on low, constant sounds, such as engines, air conditioners or the hum of a train. Sudden or high-pitched sounds, like a baby crying or a door slamming, change too quickly for the chip to follow perfectly. For this reason, most headphones also have soft, thick ear cushions that physically block higher sounds, a method known as passive noise reduction.

So the next time the world goes quiet when you put on your headphones, remember: two sounds are meeting and cancelling each other out.

groups.title: A fairer cup
groups.text:
A Fairer Cup

For most of us, coffee is simply a morning habit. Yet behind every cup is a long chain of people (farmers, traders, roasters and shop owners), and the money is rarely shared evenly. In many cases, the farmers who grow the beans receive only a small fraction of what customers finally pay.

Fair trade is one attempt to change this. Under a fair-trade system, buyers agree to pay farmers a guaranteed minimum price, even when world coffee prices fall. On top of that, they pay an extra amount, often called a premium, which farming communities decide together how to spend. In return, farmers must meet certain standards, such as limiting harmful chemicals and refusing to use child labour.

Consider the Pha Hom Growers' Group, an imaginary cooperative of 140 families in the hills of northern Thailand. Before joining a fair-trade scheme, its members sold their beans to whichever trader arrived first, often at very low prices. Today, the group sells directly to two roasters in Bangkok. Last year, its premium paid for a new drying shed and scholarships for twelve students.

Fair trade is not without its critics, however. Certification can be expensive, so the smallest farms sometimes cannot afford to join. Some economists also argue that a guaranteed price may encourage farmers to keep growing coffee even when other crops would earn them more. And because fair-trade coffee usually costs a little more in shops, its success depends on shoppers being willing to pay extra.

Still, many consumers see that extra cost as a small price for a clearer conscience. Next time you buy coffee, take a moment to read the label. It may tell you more about the journey of your drink than you expect.
